# Academic Calendar

Document ID: D01
Policy Area: Academic Calendar

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Academic Calendar governs all scheduling matters for the university. It defines the commencement of each academic term, the duration of instructional weeks, and the official semester kickoff date.

For the Fall 2026 academic term, the official commencement date for all classes is 15 September 2026. No classes will be held before this date under any circumstances.

The academic term start is followed by a full sixteen-week instructional period. Deans and department heads are responsible for communicating any local scheduling adjustments to their faculty.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Academic Calendar policy.

# Course Add and Drop

Document ID: D02
Policy Area: Course Add and Drop

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Course Add and Drop policy defines the enrollment adjustment period during which students may modify their registered courses without academic penalty.

Students are permitted to add or drop a course within 7 working days of the semester commencement. After this enrollment adjustment window closes, any change requires formal approval from the department.

The drop window is strictly enforced. Late requests are only considered in documented medical emergencies and must be routed through the registrar's office.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Course Add and Drop policy.

# Admission Application

Document ID: D03
Policy Area: Admission Application

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Admission Application policy governs the procedure and timeline for prospective students applying to undergraduate programs.

For the Fall 2026 admission cycle, the application cutoff for the Software Engineering program is 18 November 2026 at 11:59 PM. The submission portal closes precisely at this moment.

Applications received after the cutoff are automatically rejected by the system. No extensions are granted under any circumstances, including technical difficulties.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Admission Application policy.

# Assignment Submission

Document ID: D04
Policy Area: Assignment Submission

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Assignment Submission policy specifies the rules for submitting coursework and the penalties for late submissions.

Students who miss the primary deadline are granted a late submission window of 3 calendar days. During this grace period, a fixed penalty of 10% per day is applied to the final grade.

After the late submission window expires, the assignment receives a grade of zero. Instructors may not extend this period without written approval from the dean.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Assignment Submission policy.

# Class Attendance

Document ID: D05
Policy Area: Class Attendance

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Class Attendance policy establishes the minimum presence required for a student to remain in good academic standing.

Every student must maintain a minimum attendance of 75% in each registered course. Falling below this attendance threshold results in automatic disqualification from the final examination.

Attendance is recorded per class session. Medical absences with documented proof are counted separately and do not count against the student's attendance percentage.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Class Attendance policy.

# Degree Completion Requirements

Document ID: D06
Policy Area: Degree Completion Requirements

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Degree Completion Requirements policy outlines the total academic load required for the award of a bachelor's degree.

To qualify for graduation, a student must successfully complete 136 credit hours of coursework. This includes core courses, electives, and the final year project.

The degree audit is conducted in the final semester. Students who fall short of the required credit hours must register for additional courses in the following term.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Degree Completion Requirements policy.

# Disciplinary Proceedings

Document ID: D07
Policy Area: Disciplinary Proceedings

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Disciplinary Proceedings policy governs the handling of student misconduct and the process for appealing disciplinary decisions.

A student who wishes to contest a disciplinary ruling must file a formal appeal within 10 working days of receiving the official notification. The appeal window is strictly enforced.

Appeals filed after the 10 working day period are rejected without review. The disciplinary committee's decision becomes final once this deadline passes.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Disciplinary Proceedings policy.

# Final Examination

Document ID: D08
Policy Area: Final Examination

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Final Examination policy defines the passing criteria for all end-of-semester examinations.

To pass a final examination, a student must secure a minimum of 50% of the total marks. Failure to meet this passing threshold results in a failing grade for the course.

The 50% threshold applies uniformly across all departments. Supplementary examinations are offered only to students who narrowly miss the pass mark.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Final Examination policy.

# Semester Fee Structure

Document ID: D09
Policy Area: Semester Fee Structure

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Semester Fee Structure policy describes the tuition payment schedule for enrolled students.

For the fifth semester of the Software Engineering program, the semester charges are PKR 62,500. This tuition payment covers instructional costs, laboratory access, and examination fees.

The fee invoice is issued at the start of each semester. Students must clear their dues before the end of the second week to avoid a late payment surcharge.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Semester Fee Structure policy.

# Grading System

Document ID: D10
Policy Area: Grading System

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Grading System policy converts numeric scores into letter grades based on predefined boundaries.

To receive an A grade in any course, a student must obtain a grade boundary of at least 90% of the total marks. Scores between 85% and 89% fall into the A- category.

The letter grade scale is applied consistently across all semesters. Grade disputes must be raised with the instructor within one week of result announcement.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Grading System policy.

# Graduation Eligibility

Document ID: D11
Policy Area: Graduation Eligibility

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Graduation Eligibility policy defines the minimum academic standing required for degree conferral.

A student must achieve a minimum CGPA of 2.00 to be eligible for graduation. The CGPA threshold applies to the cumulative grade point average across all semesters.

Students whose CGPA falls below the graduation standing requirement must improve their grades through re-registration before applying for degree conferral.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Graduation Eligibility policy.

# Hostel Regulations

Document ID: D12
Policy Area: Hostel Regulations

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Hostel Regulations policy governs the daily conduct and timing rules for students residing in university accommodation.

All residents must return to the hostel by 10:00 PM. The hostel curfew is enforced by the residence warden, and the main gate is locked at this time.

Exceptions for late return require prior written permission from the warden. Students returning after the residence timing without permission face disciplinary action.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Hostel Regulations policy.

# Internship Requirement

Document ID: D13
Policy Area: Internship Requirement

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Internship Requirement policy outlines the industrial training component required for degree completion.

Every student must complete a minimum internship duration of 6 weeks in an approved organization. The work placement must be documented and signed by the industrial supervisor.

The industrial training is typically undertaken during the summer break. Students must submit their internship report to the department within two weeks of completing the 6 weeks duration.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Internship Requirement policy.

# Medical Leave

Document ID: D14
Policy Area: Medical Leave

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Medical Leave policy specifies the maximum health absence permitted for students during a semester.

A student may claim up to 10 days of medical leave per semester. Sick leave beyond this limit requires approval from the university medical board.

All health absence claims must be supported by a doctor's certificate. Medical leave days do not count against the regular attendance calculation.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Medical Leave policy.

# Course Prerequisites

Document ID: D15
Policy Area: Course Prerequisites

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Course Prerequisites policy defines the minimum grade required to satisfy prerequisite requirements for advanced courses.

A student must obtain at least a C grade in a prerequisite course to qualify for the dependent course. Prerequisite clearance is enforced automatically during registration.

Grades below the prerequisite grade threshold require the student to repeat the course before enrolling in the advanced course. Waivers are granted only in exceptional cases.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Course Prerequisites policy.

# Semester Registration

Document ID: D16
Policy Area: Semester Registration

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Semester Registration policy defines the minimum and maximum course load a student may register for in a semester.

The minimum registration load is 10 credit hours per semester. Students registering below this minimum enrollment are marked as part-time and may face scholarship ineligibility.

The maximum course load is 21 credit hours. Any request to exceed this limit must be approved by the academic advisor and the department chair.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Semester Registration policy.

# Merit Scholarship

Document ID: D17
Policy Area: Merit Scholarship

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Merit Scholarship policy governs the award of tuition waivers based on academic performance.

To qualify for the merit award, a student must maintain a minimum CGPA of 3.50. The scholarship eligibility is reviewed at the end of every semester.

Recipients of the tuition waiver must maintain continuous full-time enrollment. Any drop in CGPA below the scholarship eligibility threshold results in immediate termination of the award.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Merit Scholarship policy.

# Student ID Card

Document ID: D18
Policy Area: Student ID Card

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Student ID Card policy defines the procedure and processing timeline for issuing campus access cards.

The card issuance process takes 15 days from the date of application. Students must collect their identity card in person from the registrar's office.

The campus access card is required for library entry, examination halls, and laboratory access. Lost cards must be reported immediately and a replacement fee applies.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Student ID Card policy.

# Official Transcript

Document ID: D19
Policy Area: Official Transcript

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Official Transcript policy specifies the process for obtaining a certified academic record from the university.

The transcript request is processed within 5 working days of submission. Rush processing is available for an additional fee and reduces the timeline to 2 working days.

The academic record is issued in a sealed envelope and cannot be re-opened by the student. Grade reports and transcripts are mailed directly to the requesting institution.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Official Transcript policy.

# Course Withdrawal

Document ID: D20
Policy Area: Course Withdrawal

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Course Withdrawal policy defines the window during which a student may drop a course without academic penalty.

A student may withdraw from a course within 30 days of the semester start without academic penalty. The withdrawal period applies only to elective courses.

After the penalty-free drop window closes, any course cancellation appears as a W grade on the transcript. Withdrawals from core courses require advisor approval regardless of timing.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Course Withdrawal policy.

# Library Borrowing

Document ID: D21
Policy Area: Library Borrowing

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Library Borrowing policy defines the loan limits and return periods for library materials.

A student may borrow up to 5 books at a time. The book loan period is fourteen days, renewable once if no other student has placed a hold.

Overdue materials incur a fine of PKR 20 per day per book. Students with outstanding library checkout dues cannot register for the next semester.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Library Borrowing policy.

# Laboratory Safety

Document ID: D22
Policy Area: Laboratory Safety

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Laboratory Safety policy establishes mandatory precautions for all students working in university laboratories.

Safety goggles must be worn at all times inside the laboratory. Students without protective equipment are not permitted to enter or work in the lab.

Additional protective equipment such as gloves and lab coats may be required depending on the experiment. Any accident must be reported to the lab supervisor immediately.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Laboratory Safety policy.

# Plagiarism Policy

Document ID: D23
Policy Area: Plagiarism Policy

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Plagiarism Policy establishes the university's stance on academic dishonesty and the penalties for integrity violations.

Any confirmed case of plagiarism results in zero marks for the submitted work. Repeat offenses lead to suspension for one full academic semester.

All written assignments are screened through plagiarism-detection software. The integrity violation record is kept in the student's permanent academic file.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Plagiarism Policy policy.

# Annual Sports Day

Document ID: D24
Policy Area: Annual Sports Day

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Annual Sports Day policy defines the schedule and participation rules for the university's athletic events.

The sports gala will be held on 15 March each year. All students are encouraged to register for at least one athletic event.

The annual tournament includes track events, team sports, and individual competitions. Winners receive medals and a cash prize sponsored by the alumni association.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Annual Sports Day policy.

# Counselling Services

Document ID: D25
Policy Area: Counselling Services

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Counselling Services policy describes the mental health support available to enrolled students.

Each student is entitled to 8 sessions per semester with a professional counsellor at no cost. Student counselling sessions are confidential and cannot be shared without consent.

Students requiring extended mental health support beyond the 8 sessions may be referred to external specialists. All counselling records are kept separate from academic files.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Counselling Services policy.

# Course Evaluation

Document ID: D26
Policy Area: Course Evaluation

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Course Evaluation policy governs the end-of-semester feedback process for all taught courses.

Course evaluation is fully anonymous. Neither the instructor nor the department can identify individual student responses at any stage.

The feedback survey is open for two weeks before final examinations. Course review results are shared with instructors after grades are officially released.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Course Evaluation policy.

# Research Thesis

Document ID: D27
Policy Area: Research Thesis

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Research Thesis policy defines the requirements for the final year project undertaken by undergraduate students.

The research component carries a total weight of 6 credit hours, spread across the final two semesters. The thesis credits count toward the total degree requirement.

Students must submit a written thesis and defend it before a panel. The final year project grade is assigned jointly by the supervisor and the examination panel.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Research Thesis policy.

# Anti-Harassment Reporting

Document ID: D28
Policy Area: Anti-Harassment Reporting

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Anti-Harassment Reporting policy outlines the procedure for filing and processing harassment complaints on campus.

A harassment complaint must be filed within 3 days of the incident. Grievance filing after this period is only accepted with compelling justification.

All complaints are handled by the anti-harassment committee and treated with strict confidentiality. The committee must complete its inquiry within thirty days of receiving the report.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Anti-Harassment Reporting policy.

# Alumni Privileges

Document ID: D29
Policy Area: Alumni Privileges

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Alumni Privileges policy describes the benefits available to graduates of the university.

All graduates receive lifetime access to the university library and online journal databases. Alumni benefits also include discounted rates for continuing education programs.

To activate alumni benefits, graduates must register with the alumni office and obtain an alumni card. Graduate services are extended to all degree holders regardless of graduation year.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Alumni Privileges policy.

# Transport Services

Document ID: D30
Policy Area: Transport Services

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Transport Services policy defines the bus service routes and charges for students using university transportation.

The annual transport charges for the campus shuttle are PKR 15,000. The bus service operates on ten fixed routes across the city.

Transport charges are billed with the semester fee. Students may discontinue the campus shuttle service at the end of any semester by submitting a written request.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End of Transport Services policy.
